idiom_name: Selenide page()/open() from Kotlin plus delegated lazy element properties
implementation_notes: Kotlin uses the JVM drivers through ordinary interop: Selenide's page objects compile almost unchanged from Kotlin (no PageFactory, no initElements), with the one Kotlin wart that Selenide's $ and $$ functions must be called in backticks because Kotlin identifiers cannot contain a dollar sign, and Kotlin adds idioms of its own - elements can be exposed as `val query by lazy { ... }`, methods can be expression-bodied, and data classes carry the values scraped from a page. open(url, Page::class.java) and page(ResultsPage::class.java) cover navigation while Selenide's proxies handle waiting. Choose it where the suite is Selenide-oriented; the Playwright variant otherwise.
pitfalls: by lazy caches the proxy on first access, not the element: proxies re-resolve, but a lazily captured element or a value read from one is stale after navigation.
Java interop exposes platform types (String!) whose nullability Kotlin cannot verify: a page method returning a Java API's possibly-null value must declare the real nullable type.
Selenide's page()/open() are bound to the current thread's WebDriver; sharing one page object across parallel coroutines or threads breaks the implicit driver binding.

variants.name: Playwright for Java driven from Kotlin (typed Page/Locator)
variants.idiom_name: com.microsoft.playwright.Page/Locator wrapped in a Kotlin class
variants.implementation_notes: Playwright's Java binding is used from Kotlin like any other JVM library: the page class takes Page in its constructor, keeps Locator fields (val input: Locator = page.locator("[aria-label='Enter your search term']")), and exposes methods calling fill/press/click; locators are lazy and auto-waiting, so no explicit waits hide in the class. Kotlin adds null-safety around the binding's platform types and lets navigation methods return the next page type. Choose it when the suite is Playwright-based rather than Selenide.
pitfalls: Playwright objects are not thread-safe: a page object must stay on the thread that created the browser context, so sharing it with coroutines on other dispatchers fails.
Java getters returning platform types (Locator?) invite accidental !!; model absence explicitly instead of silencing the type system.
